description:
Design the mechanical classifier that decides whether a proposed change is upstreamable or fork-local. Primary signal: git diff against the upstream main commit the user installed from. Files untouched vs. upstream = upstreamable surface; files diverged = fork-local.

Must handle:
- Public forks (normal case)
- Private forks (auto-detect and default off; user can enable explicitly)
- Detached installs (no upstream remote)
- Stale upstream refs (user hasn't pulled in a while)
- Partial overlap (change touches both diverged and pristine files — split or reject?)

Deliverable: conclusion.md with the classifier contract, edge-case disposition table, and a go/no-go on whether git-diff alone is sufficient or whether file-level fingerprinting is also required.
name: upstream-divergence-classifier
title: Design upstream-divergence classifier for contribution eligibility
